newsitem.title: USA: Ohio's soil moisture improves, still 49 pct short.
newsitem.headline: Ohio's soil moisture improves, still 49 pct short.

text.p: Topsoil moisture conditions improved last week, but nearly half of the state's topsoil moisture was still rated short or very short, the Ohio Agricultural Statistics Service said on Monday.
Topsoil moisture was rated 49 percent short to very short, compared with 84 percent the previous week.
Corn was rated five percent very poor, 16 percent poor, 40 percent fair, 35 good and four percent excellent.
Two percent of the corn crop has matured, but only a fraction of a percent has been harvested. Normally, one fourth of the crop is mature by now and two percent harvested.
Ninety-two percent of the corn had reached the dough stage, behind the five-year average of 100 percent. Forty-three percent was dented versus 88 percent average.
Soybeans were rated four percent very poor, 16 percent poor, 42 fair, 33 percent good and five percent excellent.
A small fraction of the soybean crop had been harvested, but only 14 percent were dropping leaves, well behind the 51-percent average.
Winter wheat seeding matched the average of one percent.
Pasture was rated nine percent very poor, 22 percent poor, 41 percent fair, 25 percent good and three percent excellent.
